[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''', written '''Will''' in the derivative chronology, was recorded in 1730 as a son of '''[[Glasgow-1504|James Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Murray-20395|Sarah or Sara Murray]]''' in the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian register.<ref name="Chronology">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html "Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context"], 1730 household entry and distinct-person list.</ref>

The public Emerald Ancestors index independently lists a male William Glasgow in County Antrim in 1730.<ref>[https://www.emeraldancestors.com/northern-ireland-ancestry-search-birth-list?County=Antrim&Forenames=&Surname=Gillis&brideforenames=&bridesurname=&civildistrict=&searchtype= Emerald Ancestors, County Antrim birth index], William Glasgow, 1730.</ref>

A William Glasgow appears among the Larne-area inhabitants who signed a published petition against the Hearts of Steel in April 1772.<ref>[https://www.kinsleuth.com/belnews/1770-1779.htm Blair extracts from the ''Belfast News-Letter'', 1770–1779], 7 April 1772, p. 3, Larne, Kilwaughter and Raloo petition.</ref> The chronology identifies the signer as the William born in 1730. This is a reasonable same-name and locality match, but the newspaper supplies no age or relatives.

A Connor wills index lists '''William Glasgow of Larne''' in 1783.<ref>[https://studylib.net/doc/7083819/general-information-series "Family History Guide: Inver, Kilwaughter and Larne Parishes"], Diocese of Connor wills index, William Glasgow of Larne, 1783.</ref> The entry may belong to this William or to the older [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]]; it cannot presently be assigned securely.

== Research Notes ==
The chronology's distinct-person list reports that [[Glasgow-3986|James Glasgow]], born about 1775, was buried on the same St Cedma's stone as this William.<ref name="Chronology" /> A different passage on the same page associates James with William born about 1708. The complete inscription has not been recovered, and a shared memorial would not by itself distinguish a son, grandson or collateral relative. James is therefore a useful descendant lead, not a proved child of this William.

No inspected record identifies William's wife or children.

Registry of Deeds memorial 62131 names an adult William Glasgow as an adjoining Larne occupier in March 1736. That occurrence cannot be this William, who was only about six, and belongs to the older Larne identity represented by [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]].

The original Larne and Kilwaughter register survives at PRONI under reference ''MIC/1B/6''. Its marriage and baptism entries should be searched before 1769 for William's household.

=== Unidentified William Glasgow, deed witness in 1772 ===
A lease dated 12 May 1772 from John Miller, currier of Gardenmore in Old Town of Larne, to David Drennan, weaver, names Wm Glasgow, David Dickey and James Fairies, all of Larne, as witnesses. Either [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] or [[Glasgow-3326|William Glasgow]] could be this witness; the deed gives no age, occupation or relative to distinguish them. The son William named in the trust clause is Drennan's son, not a Glasgow relationship. Registration on 9 November 1784 does not prove that the witness William Glasgow was still alive then.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Miller to Drennan, lease 12 May 1772, registered 9 November 1784, manuscript p. 315, image 166; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-SQLT-3 original image], inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

=== Possible Captain Glasgow, vessel William at New-York, 1758 ===
A February 1758 shipping report lists the vessel William, master Glasgow, from London, at New-York.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/34419759/ The Public Advertiser, 1758-02-18, p.1].</ref>

William is the vessel’s name; the master’s personal forename is not stated. The voyage does not identify his residence, birthplace or family.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3326]]. Uncertain 1730 Kilwaughter birth permits an adult in 1758. Personal forename is unknown in the notice; no maritime, voyage or family connection.

=== Possible William Glascoe / Glascow, 1760 defendant ===
William Glascoe is among prisoners reported sentenced to transportation after Old Bailey trials, for stealing a sack of malt from a warehouse, valued in the newspaper at £4 10s.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/35690357/ Public Ledger or Daily Register of Commerce and Intelligence, 1760-04-18, p.2].</ref>

The newspaper uses Glascoe; the associated Old Bailey case uses Glascow. The case association does not establish the defendant’s origin, family or identity with the later Maryland man.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3326]]. The recorded 1730 birth at Kilwaughter, Larne, County Antrim, Ireland is chronologically compatible. The newspaper gives no family or individual identifier connecting this occurrence to Glasgow-3326.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Philadelphia and Charles-Town postal lists, 1759–1771 ===
William Glasgow, Cecil County, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39399295/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1759-08-09, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in February 1763.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39390517/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1763-02-24, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in October 1765.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39405824/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1765-10-10, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow is separately listed in the Charles-Town, Maryland, post-office letters notice headed 1 October 1771, beside an entry for John Glasgow of West Nottingham.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41041559/ Maryland Gazette, 1771-10-24, p.3].</ref>

Cecil County explicitly qualifies the 1759 entry only. In 1763 "Pennsylvania" follows James Gillispie; in 1765 "Forks of Delaware" qualifies William Greenlee, not William Glasgow. The entries may concern different men, and co-listing with John in 1771 does not prove a family relationship.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3326]]. Uncertain 1730 birth, Kilwaughter/Larne, is compatible; no postal or Cecil County connection.
